subtype: Raised shoulders as fear or cold [Interpreting]
passage: "You look so sure of yourself when you read people, Pema," Ira said, pouring tea for her niece. "Let me tell you about the time I was wrong. I was twenty, standing at a bus stop in the early morning. A young man beside me had his shoulders pulled up near his ears, and he kept glancing round. I thought, he's frightened, someone must be after him. I even took a step toward the shopkeeper for help." She laughed. "Then I asked, 'Are you all right?' He said, 'It's freezing, and I forgot my jacket.' I wanted to vanish." Pema grinned. "So?" "So now I read the weather and the situation before I read the person. And if I'm unsure, I ask."

qa.q: Where was Ira standing when she saw the young man?
qa.a: She was standing at a bus stop in the early morning.

qa.q: What did Ira think when she saw his shoulders pulled up?
qa.a: She thought he was frightened and that someone might be after him, though he was only cold.

qa.q: What does Ira do now when she sees someone with raised shoulders?
qa.a: She considers the weather and the situation first, and asks if she is unsure.

qa.q: How might the young man have felt when Ira asked if he was all right?
qa.a: He was probably a little surprised and perhaps touched at her concern, even though the truth was only the cold.

grounding: A young adult sees raised shoulders and guesses fear, though it was cold, so context and asking come first.

subtype: Raised shoulders as fear or cold [Interpreting]
passage: The power had been out in the hostel since afternoon, and a cold wind rattled the shutters. In the corridor Chaitanya spotted Lalit with his shoulders hunched up around his ears, staring at the floor, his phone dead in his hand. Chaitanya's mind jumped: exam results were due today, so Lalit must be afraid. He almost started a pep talk about not worrying. Then he noticed his own arms crossed against the chill, and Lalit's thin shirt. It was dark and freezing. He took a step closer and said, "Hey, you all right? Or is it just cold?" Lalit gave a short laugh. "Just cold. I left my sweater at the canteen." Chaitanya lent him his blanket.

qa.a: A cold wind was rattling the shutters.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya first afraid Lalit was feeling?
qa.a: He first guessed that Lalit was fearful about the exam results, reading the hunched shoulders as worry.
He offered both possibilities, worry or just cold, so Lalit could tell him the truth without feeling put on the spot.

qa.q: How might Lalit have felt if Chaitanya had given a pep talk?
qa.a: He might have felt confused or a bit embarrassed, since he wasn't worried at all and only needed warmth.

grounding: A young adult sees raised shoulders and guesses fear, though it may only be cold, so context and asking come first.
